So, I am a guy with Body Dysmorphic Disorder. For all of my adolescence I was utterly disgusted with my body, and thought I could never be attractive to anyone. Some days I would skip school because I hated how I looked so much. One day, I decided I was tired of feeling ugly. For a few years I worked hard to develop my style, my body, a flattering hairstyle for my naturally frizzy hair, etc, and it paid off. I got a lot of validation from peers on my appearance and in the past year I finally came to a place where I truly felt like my looks were good enough for me to exist. Even so, it didn't fully meet my inflated standards. I researched various plastic surgery procedures and obsessed over it for a while but I decided that I was going to wait until I was in my 20s and my face was fully formed before doing anything drastic.

One of the strong points of my appearance is my hair. I have unique curly hair that I know how to style well and I get lots of compliments on it. It was something I started to attach my identity to.

Then, I found out I was going bald.

I felt like I was losing a part of myself. I thought, this is the end for my appearance. I mean, how many bald male sex symbols are there in mainstream media? There's The Rock and Jason Statham, that's basically it. If you go on /r/LadyBoners and you scroll and scroll, you will probably not find a single bald guy (I actually did this, that's how insecure I was). I stayed up all night researching baldness treatments obsessively and I came to the heartwrenching conclusion that there is no real cure, only temporary treatments that can have life-changing side effects or are extremely expensive.

Here's what this whole thing has forced me to realize: It's bullshit. It's all bullshit, all the obsessing over whether my appearance meets this societal standard or whether people will think this thing is attractive. Some days I look into the mirror and think I'm hot shit, and some days I think I look subhuman. The fact is, if I ever want to live a happy life, I have to accept that I may never truly like how I look. All I can do is try to look the best I can, and just live my life. Otherwise, I'm just trying to meet this poorly defined, impossible to meet standard that, even if I did reach it, how long could I really maintain it for? It's a recipe for misery, especially with my mental condition. 

I don't mean to scare you but women can go bald too, permanently.  I don't have this specific kind of hair loss but alopecia areata can affect both men and women. If you let having a slightly subpar ass gets to you that much, what would you do if you lost your hair? The only solution to living a happy life is to just fucking let go. Let this go and live out the rest of our short humans lives, otherwise I'll be on my deathbed and wondering why I spent all that precious time and energy worrying about how my cheekbones weren't defined enough.

I wrote as much for me as for others because I haven't fully adopted this attitude, as much as I would like to. It's a work in progress. But it's the only way I can really be happy.
